name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean in a heavily Republican Missouri seat
Open seat removes incumbent risk but no competitive dynamics emerged
Republican Stigall has a large fundraising edge over Democrat Smead
Prediction markets price the Republican at ~95%
model.rationale: The R+19 lean and a favorable environment make this a safe Republican open seat; Stigall's fundraising advantage and markets pricing near 95% reinforce that. No polls or expert ratings show any sign of a competitive race.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a Republican primary-style misstep could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
MO-06 is a heavily Republican northwest Missouri district that Sam Graves held for decades; his retirement creates an open seat but does not change the underlying partisan math. The district's R+19 lean and a favorable national environment for Republicans point to a comfortable Republican hold.

Republican Chris Stigall has outraised Democrat Josh Smead by roughly eight to one, and outside groups have spent against the Democrat while ignoring the Republican side. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 95% chance, and no public polls or expert ratings suggest the race is competitive. The forecast is a Safe Republican hold with a margin in the high teens.
